chapter: War years, Goodman and Woody Herman
title: Small band on 52nd Street with Billie Holiday and young Shorty Rogers
summary: At the Downbeat Club he led seven pieces, including 17-year-olds Shorty Rogers and Eddie Bert, but the record ban prevented recording.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then I went up to the country, Mildred and I Had a place up at [Kent Close] --
Up near the Viaduct there, up near Pough-keepsie.
But I think you've been up there.
-- Could go up by boat, couldn't you?
Couldn't you go up the Hudson?
No, we drove up, we drove up.

Then, it was during this period that -- that I started a small band. And I'd be -- met Eddie Bert down at the Village and we'd become friends. And so I formed a little band and we went to a job on 52nd Street. AT the Downbeat Club, I think it was. And we went in with Billie Holiday. I had Shorty Rogers, Eddie Bert, Aaron Sax, Hank Kahout, Specs Powell, Clyde Lombardi.
And it was a great band. We had some great things, it was very disappointing because there was a
record ban on during that time and we never recorded that band.

We did make some after we closed down there. One engagement there, and we went out -- we went oh, to Detroit and some more places. We went to a party down at George Simon, he recorded something, a home recording --
Piano was out of tune and everything, but the playing was good, pretty good. But we never really got to make anything with that one. It was a wonderful little band.
Had Shorty Rogers been doing a lot of work, at that time, by then.
No. He was 17 and so was Eddie Bert.
That's what I thought. Where did you --
